Implemented RED-first per the plan.

RED (against the tree, before the fix), 3 new tests failing:
- test_pass1_ladder_retry_stays_on_the_run_s_own_bedrock_model:
  observed retry models ['claude-opus-4-8', 'claude-opus-4-8'] !=
  ['bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8-v1:0', ...]
- test_models_at_or_above_keeps_a_bedrock_primary_on_bedrock_with_no_classes:
  ['claude-opus-4-8'] != ['bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8-v1:0']
- test_models_at_or_above_drops_unnameable_higher_rungs:
  ['claude-haiku-4-5','claude-sonnet-4-6','claude-opus-4-8'] !=
  ['bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-v1:0']

The two guard tests (the _too_big failure-path case and the out-of-scope start-rung
pin for a non-Anthropic FAMILY primary) were green before and after, as intended.

Fix: _rung_target now takes the run's primary model plus an own_rung flag and returns
str | None. It resolves the rung through its class exactly as before, then compares
infer_provider(primary) with infer_provider(target): agree or either undeterminable ->
today's value byte-for-byte; differ on the primary's own rung -> the primary verbatim;
differ on a higher rung -> None, dropped. models_at_or_above threads the primary on the
located-start-rung branch only and filters the Nones; the no-match fallback is unchanged.

MODEL_LADDER and largest_window_tokens are untouched, so escalation WINDOWS stay keyed on
concrete families while escalation TARGETS move to the class vocabulary.

Every pre-existing test is unmodified: git diff on tests/ is 93 insertions, 0 deletions.
make lint exit 0, make typecheck exit 0 (mypy clean, 411 files).

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

A plan review that trips a provider context limit escalates the Pass-1 finder onto a model the
run was never configured for. On a run whose model is provider-qualified for anything other than
the provider inferred from the model NAME — a Bedrock deployment being the live case — the
recovery path silently relocates the call to direct Anthropic: a hard failure in a
provider-isolated container, or unbudgeted spend wherever an Anthropic key happens to exist.
This is the founding defect of epic 061c on a second, independent code path: the ENTRY rung was
routed through the model-class vocabulary, the ESCALATION rungs were not.

Confirmed by running the function on this tree with no class table configured:

    models_at_or_above("bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8-v1:0")
      -> ["claude-opus-4-8"]        # bare, direct-Anthropic-inferring

## Root cause

`_rung_target` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py:332-359`) decides a rung's escalation target
by comparing the RUNG's own provider-inferred form against that rung's class resolution:

    resolved = resolve_model_string(class_name)       # sizing.py:354
    provider = infer_provider(bare)                   # sizing.py:355
    own = f"{provider}:{bare}" if provider else bare  # sizing.py:356
    return bare if resolved == own else resolved      # sizing.py:357

Both sides of that comparison are derived from the ladder constant. **The model the run is
actually on is never an input.** So whenever the class table has not been retargeted the equality
holds and the rung degrades to `MODEL_LADDER`'s bare Anthropic family name
(`sizing.py:99-103`), discarding whatever provider qualifier `cfg.model` carried.
`models_at_or_above` (`sizing.py:362-376`) hands those targets to the escalation loop, which
assigns them straight onto the run config at `sizing.py:427-431`:

    for model in models_at_or_above(cfg.model):
        passes.pass1_chunk(runner, replace(cfg, model=model), ...)

Two consequences, both reproduced against the current tree:

1. A Bedrock-qualified primary escalates to a bare Anthropic id (transcript above).
   `cfg.model_provider` (`src/rebar/llm/config.py:391`) is left untouched by `replace`, so a run
   that qualified through that field instead composes an id like `bedrock:claude-opus-4-8`,
   which is not a valid Bedrock model id.
2. The Pass-1 entry rung names `frontier` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py:76`, resolved
   at `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/production_batch_runner.py:97-100`), so
   `models_at_or_above("anthropic:claude-opus-4-8")` returns the single-element list
   `["claude-opus-4-8"]`. The substitution therefore executes on the COMMON one-criterion retry,
   before any escalation is needed — it is not confined to a rare deep-escalation case.

When a class table IS configured for another provider the current code is already correct
(`models_at_or_above` returns the Bedrock ladder, asserted at
`tests/unit/test_model_class_ladder.py:204-212`). The live gap is the UNCONFIGURED-table plus
provider-qualified-`cfg.model` combination, which no test covers.

## Approach

Make the rung target a function of the model the run is on, and make the unnameable case fail
SAFE instead of crossing providers.

`models_at_or_above` already holds the primary, so thread it into `_rung_target`. Resolve the
rung through its model class exactly as today, then compare the RUN's provider
(`infer_provider(primary)`) with the TARGET's provider (`infer_provider(target)`):

- providers agree, or either is undeterminable -> return today's value byte-for-byte;
- providers differ and the rung is the PRIMARY's OWN rung -> return `primary` verbatim, so the
  same-model one-criterion retry still runs on the operator's model (that retry is the step that
  most often succeeds, since one criterion is a far smaller prompt than the batch);
- providers differ on a HIGHER rung -> drop the rung. The class vocabulary is the only thing
  that can name that rung in the run's provider and it has not been configured, so there is no
  honest target. Escalation stops and the existing too-big failure finding
  (`sizing.py:450-471`) reports it — a visible outcome instead of a silent provider jump.

The rule applies only on the branch that LOCATED a start rung (`sizing.py:373-375`). The
no-match fallback (`sizing.py:376`) is left exactly as today, because without a located start
rung there is no "primary's own rung" to preserve; see Scope for why that branch is out of scope.

Why this approach fits: the defect is that a decision about the CURRENT run is made from module
constants alone, so the fix is to give the decision the run's model — the smallest input that
makes the question answerable. It keeps the model-class vocabulary as the single source of
escalation targets (the epic's rule) while preserving the byte-for-byte back-compat that the
docstring at `sizing.py:335-347` exists to protect, so no existing caller's strings change.

Deliberately NOT changed: on an unqualified or Anthropic-qualified primary the target stays the
bare form (`anthropic:claude-opus-4-8` -> `claude-opus-4-8`). That substitution is byte-different
but provider-identical. The harm was never the bare FORM; it was the provider CHANGE, and the
provider-agreement rule is what removes that. Preserving the bare form is the back-compat
contract that keeps `tests/unit/test_plan_review.py:1145-1150` and
`tests/unit/test_model_class_ladder.py:256-271` passing unmodified.

`MODEL_LADDER` also keeps its bare family names. It carries two roles and only one moves: it is
also the WINDOW table that `largest_window_tokens` (`sizing.py:137-146`) reads by substring match
(`if name in model`), which is why `sizing.py:319-324` records that class names in that table
would make every window lookup miss. Escalation TARGETS move to the class vocabulary; escalation
WINDOWS stay keyed on concrete model families. That separates the two orderings the constant
conflates without splitting the constant.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py` — `_rung_target` takes the primary model as an argument
  and applies the provider-agreement rule; `models_at_or_above` passes it on the located-start-rung
  branch. No other function in the file changes.
- `tests/unit/test_model_class_ladder.py` — new cases (see Testing). This is the existing home of
  the ladder's model-class contract, holding both the byte-for-byte control (lines 256-271) and
  the configured-Bedrock case (lines 204-212) this change must not disturb.

Explicitly OUT of scope, to be raised as a separate ticket: `models_at_or_above` locates the START
rung by substring-matching `MODEL_LADDER`'s Anthropic family names against the primary
(`sizing.py:373-374`), so a primary from another model family falls through to the whole ladder
beginning at the trivial rung — confirmed on this tree:
`models_at_or_above("bedrock:us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0")` returns all three Anthropic rungs, so a
context-limit escalation would DOWNGRADE the window. `largest_window_tokens` has the matching gap,
returning the ladder maximum (1,000,000) for that same primary. That is a different mechanism —
rung LOCATION, not rung TARGET — and this change leaves it byte-for-byte as it is.

## Testing

New cases in `tests/unit/test_model_class_ladder.py`, using its existing `no_classes` and
`_set_class_table` fixtures.

- **The defect, on the escalation path itself** — not on `models_at_or_above` in isolation. Drive
  `sizing.pass1_with_ladder` with a stub runner whose first (batch) call raises a context-limit
  error (`is_context_limit_error`, `sizing.py:300-316`, matches the substring
  `"prompt is too long"`) and a `cfg` whose model is `bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8-v1:0`
  with no class table. Assert the `cfg.model` observed by the one-criterion retry call is that
  exact string. This is the case an entry-rung test structurally cannot catch, which is why the
  defect survived the entry-rung fix.
- **Worked example, unit level** — with no class table:
  `models_at_or_above("bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8-v1:0")` returns
  `["bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8-v1:0"]`. Today it returns `["claude-opus-4-8"]`.
- **Edge, higher rungs are dropped rather than crossed** — with no class table:
  `models_at_or_above("bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-v1:0")` returns exactly
  `["bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-v1:0"]`, and no returned element contains
  `claude-sonnet` or `claude-opus`.
- **Edge, escalation still reports the size failure** — the same Bedrock-haiku primary under a
  runner that raises a context-limit error at every attempt still yields the existing `_too_big`
  failure finding (`sizing.py:450-471`) rather than an empty result or a raised exception.
- **Back-compat controls, kept passing unmodified** — the byte-for-byte case
  (`tests/unit/test_model_class_ladder.py:256-271`, covering bare rungs, `None`, and
  `"some-unknown-model"`), the order case (lines 275-299), the configured-Bedrock case
  (lines 204-212), and `orchestrator._models_at_or_above`'s literal assertions
  (`tests/unit/test_plan_review.py:1145-1150`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With no model-class table configured and a primary of
      `bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8-v1:0`, the model that reaches `passes.pass1_chunk` on
      the one-criterion retry is that same string; verified by the new `pass1_with_ladder` test
      asserting the observed `cfg.model`, which fails against the current tree.
- [ ] No escalation target is returned whose inferred provider differs from the primary's
      inferred provider when both are determinable; verified by a test asserting
      `models_at_or_above("bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-v1:0")` equals
      `["bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-v1:0"]` under the `no_classes` fixture.
- [ ] Dropping unnameable higher rungs does not turn escalation into a crash or a silent empty
      result: the all-attempts-fail case still produces the `_too_big` failure finding; verified
      by the new failure-path test asserting `finding["_too_big"] is True`.
- [ ] Escalation targets still come from the model-class vocabulary when a class table IS
      configured; verified by `test_models_at_or_above_stays_on_bedrock_for_a_bedrock_primary`
      (`tests/unit/test_model_class_ladder.py:204`) passing unmodified.
- [ ] The window sizes that drive the escalation DECISION are unchanged; verified by `git diff`
      showing no change to `MODEL_LADDER` (`sizing.py:99-103`) or `largest_window_tokens`
      (`sizing.py:137-146`).
- [ ] Back-compat: with no class table configured, every escalation target for an unqualified or
      Anthropic-qualified primary is today's value byte-for-byte, including the
      `anthropic:claude-opus-4-8` common path that yields bare `claude-opus-4-8`; verified by
      `test_models_at_or_above_returns_todays_bare_ids_with_no_classes_configured` and
      `test_models_at_or_above_escalation_order_is_unchanged` passing unmodified.
- [ ] The out-of-scope start-rung behaviour is untouched:
      `models_at_or_above("bedrock:us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0")` still returns the three bare
      Anthropic rungs; verified by a pinning test asserting that exact list.
- [ ] `pytest tests/unit/test_model_class_ladder.py tests/unit/test_plan_review.py
      tests/unit/workflow/test_pass1_usage.py tests/unit/test_llm_failure_matrix.py` passes, and
      `make lint` and `make typecheck` are clean.
